title: 대화에서 한마디 더: 맛있어요. 싸고요.
objective: By the end, you can add one more fact to your answer in a conversation with -고요. You will use the correct form after verbs, adjectives, past tense, and nouns.
summary: Learn to use the sentence ending -고요 to add one more piece of information after you have already answered.

task.title: Add one more thing
task.line: First say one complete sentence, then add more with -고요. Fill in, fix, choose, or answer as each item asks.

forms.when: After any verb or adjective stem, with or without a final consonant
forms.means: Adds one more fact to what you just said: "…and also ~."
forms.example: A: 이 카페 어때요? B: 커피가 맛있어요. 조용하고요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: How is this café? B: The coffee is good. And it's quiet, too.

forms.when: When the added fact happened in the past
forms.means: Adds one more thing you did or that happened: "…and I also did ~."
forms.example: A: 주말에 뭐 했어요? B: 친구를 만났어요. 같이 영화도 봤고요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: What did you do on the weekend? B: I met a friend. We also saw a movie together.

forms.when: After a noun ending in a final consonant
forms.means: Adds one more fact about who or what something is
forms.example: A: 마크 씨는 어느 나라 사람이에요? B: 미국 사람이에요. 회사원이고요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: Where is Mark from? B: He's American. And he's an office worker.

forms.when: After a noun ending in a vowel (이고요 is also correct)
forms.means: Adds one more fact about who or what something is
forms.example: A: 그분은 누구예요? B: 제 누나예요. 의사고요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: Who is that? B: She's my older sister. And she's a doctor.

watchOut: 비싸요고요 (X) → 비싸고요 (O): Add -고요 to the stem, not to the -요 form.
선생님고요 (X) → 선생님이고요 (O): After a final consonant, use 이고요.
어제 쇼핑했어요. 옷도 사고요. (X) → 옷도 샀고요. (O): If the added fact is in the past, use the past form.
B: 멀고요. (X) as a first answer → B: 멀어요. 크고요. (O): Give one full answer first, then add more with -고요.
exercises: Fill in the blank with -고요 (넓다): A: 새 집이 어때요? B: 방이 커요. 부엌도 ____.
Fill in the blank with -고요 in the past (찍다): A: 어제 뭐 했어요? B: 공원에서 산책했어요. 사진도 많이 ____.
Write 이고요 or 고요: ① 제 동생은 대학생이에요. 스무 살____. ② 이 사람은 제 남편이에요. 가수____.
Find and fix the mistake: 친구 집은 조용해요. 깨끗해요고요.
Choose the natural answer: A: 한국어 수업이 어때요? ① 재미있고요. 쉬워요. ② 재미있어요. 쉽고요.
Answer in Korean with two sentences. End the second one with -고요 (cheap / many people): A: 그 시장이 어때요?
answers: ① 이고요 ② 고요 (이고요 is also correct)
재미있어요. 쉽고요. (Answer with a complete -어요 sentence first, then add one more fact with -고요.)
